records.rationale: The declaration token is the interface method member IHandler.Handle (Handlers.cs 0-indexed line 6, chars 11-17). I enumerated every exact 'Handle' identifier token across the three source files (all other grep hits are substrings inside IHandler, ConsoleHandler, BufferHandler, HandlerFactory, or HandlerExtensions and were omitted). Exactly two tokens semantically resolve to the interface declaration: the two invocations whose receivers are statically typed as IHandler (Consumers.cs line 15 and Polymorphism.cs line 25). The two implicit implementation declarations (ConsoleHandler.Handle, BufferHandler.Handle) declare distinct symbols that implement the interface member, and the three invocations through concrete receivers (ConsoleHandler and BufferHandler variables) statically bind to those implementation symbols; all five were inspected and proven to resolve elsewhere, so they are excluded rather than required. No C# using/import binding token names the member Handle (the WorkerAlias using-alias binds ConsoleHandler, not Handle), so no optional binding locations exist. definitionUsage is the URI/position-sorted first required location. All source lines are ASCII, so UTF-16 columns equal byte columns. The required set is complete with no unresolved required-contract ambiguity.
